[quote=karcovshkie;60015920][spoiler=Appetizer (1781W)]

The swarm begins its venture to satiate its great hunger, multiple hive ships begin channeling. A great rift tears through space and time as their psionic power is unleashed. A rift, nearly the size of a continent, is formed. The hive ships move into the rift disappearing into nothingness on their hunt. The rift closes as the last of the seven hive ships enters. In the cosmic rift bright beams of energy illuminate the hive ships' paths, a light shining as bright as the sun draws them in like moths to a flame, this light is the lifeforce of the people living on the planet Scoria a system unfortunately close to vorax space, this is the light of their souls, their emotions. The hive ships begin wading through the cosmic rift moving at speeds faster than light as they near the unknowing populace of Scoria. Scoria is home to a small colony of inhabitants from a shattered star empire, they are on their own out here. The cosmic rift is rough and takes a great toll on the hive ships, lashing out with energy made from emotions, storms of lost souls and anger swirl throughout the cosmic rift, but the hive ships have grown accustomed to this way of travel their thick hides equal to that of the strongest durasteel plating on star cruisers, they travel with little care for the tempests that rage around them. Time and space move much differently here in the cosmic rift, what would be light years at light speed takes the vorax only two days. They have reached the Delthus solar system, and are in range of Scoria. The rift begins to rip open once more, energy of the rift pours out into deep space as the vorax hive ships emerge through the hole in reality itself. The hive ships have seemingly appeared out of thin air. To the people on Scoria there were no signs of FTL warp drives, only a large solar storm which lasted for nearly thirty minutes before the hive ships emerged. Multiple unclassified bioforms were being picked up on screen, sizes ranging from seven to ten kilometers in length. These lumbering giants moved upon the planet big and slow as they approached. The planet's militum began to ready itself, they saw what was coming. Orbital gauss turrets, and flak cannons trained on their targets, missile pods began launching their salvos. Any and all starfighters were scrambled immediately, bombers, fighters, interceptors, anything with space fairing capabilities was deployed. Multiple cruisers began moving to intercept, but they were far out on the other side of the planet. The hive ships pressed on, missiles making their mark slamming into the thick carapace of the hive ships. The gauss turrets and flak cannons open fire, but the gauss rounds do little with the hive ships not even feeling the flak. The vorax hive ships are in range, and the vanguard start to release their many, many flyers. The flak tears apart the flyers but for every flyer killed ten more take its place. It's like a cloud of flesh moving uncaring for the defenders' desperate attempts. The star fighters are almost instantly overwhelmed by the voraxs' numbers, as they fall so do the planetary defense platforms, one hive ship rams straight through one of the platforms splitting it in two. Way above the sky a huge shadow is cast down upon the inhabitants of the world, clouds of skin and bones dot the sky, as massive bodies blot out the sun. In orbit the hive ships sit, over the planet's horizon approaches two cruisers Helios, and her sister ship Phanes. They get into range and begin to fire at the hive ships, but they are woefully outnumbered. Rounds connect and form cracks in the closest hive ship's armor, but the swarm of flyers begin to creep up upon the cruisers. The vorax hive ships in range begin launching spore clusters at the cruisers. These are large clumps of vorax creatures filled with vesper, a volatile liquid capable of causing devastating explosions when it reacts to certain chemicals found inside vorax spores. The cruisers open fire on the incoming flyers shredding through hundreds before they ever get close to the ships, but their numbers seem endless. Before the flyers reach the Helios, a spore cluster slams into the bow of the ship, ripping apart multiple decks, and sublevels within the ship. The front of the ship splintered many of the deck guns either blown up completely or torn from the hull by the blast. The ship continues to fire despite its shields totally failing and hull integrity at sixty eight percent. The flyers then make impact, now with multiple layers of the ship peeled back they begin to seep into the wounds of the ship. A second spore cluster approaches but detonates prematurely off the starboard side rocking the vessel but not causing any damage, it doesn't need to. The flyers have already entered the ship and have begun consuming it from the inside out. A third spore cluster hits the ship impacting the bridge. Her sister ship Phanes loses contact with the Helios. The ship begins to drift aimlessly and starts to fall out of orbit down to the planet's surface. The flyers and hive ships now turn their attention to the Phanes. The Phanes now alone and hopelessly outmatched begins its final stand. Deck guns ring out, vibrating through the cruisers hull. Rounds bore through the swarms of flyers and slam into the closest hive ship, the projectiles burrow into the hive ships flesh before exploding, sending chunks of armor and flesh careening throughout space. Blood spurts from the holes made in the hive ships skin. The hive ship fires off multiple spore clusters, knowing the devastation they cause the cruiser focuses fire upon the clusters. They explode killing many flyers in proximity, one gets close to the portside before exploding violently, rocking the cruiser causing many aboard to lose their balance. The flyers outside the ship are like bugs on a windshield, it's impossible to have a visual on the hive ships, but their massive bio signatures cannot be hidden. The flyers coat the ship in a layer of flesh biting and clawing at the ship's exterior. The shields hold strong despite their relentless assault, and the cruiser keeps firing, cleaving through the swarms of flyers as rounds make impact with one the hive ships. The hive ship feels this great pain, a throbbing headache for the gigantic creature, it begins to charge angered by the resilience of this prey. Rounds from the cruiser slam into the front of the hive ship. Some bounce while others lodge into the flesh and detonate, the Phanes then has a sudden loss of power. It was only momentary, lights flickered on and off for just a brief second, but to what caused it the crew didn't know, and then multiple warning messages were being displayed. Ion engines began to heat up, something was starting to block or clog their propulsion. At the aft of the ship vorax flyers began throwing themselves into the engines, causing damage to their components but also started to clog the engines with their bodies. Flesh burned and the bones started to char but with so much biomass being thrown into the engines they simply started to overheat. Eventually all power to the engines was lost, as the engines themselves overheated and internal components began to melt and fuse together. The Phanes is now drifting, the hive ship grows ever closer, with the Phanes still firing, the hive ship opens its maw and bites down on the ship. Multiple decks are sheared instantly, power from the ship drains, lights flicker before being snuffed out, and the vorax hive ship consumes the rest of the Phanes. On the surface the helios is seen, its reentry into the atmosphere makes it glow bright orange, chunks of the ship tear off from the main body as it descends, what left of the ship crashes hard into the soil of Scoria, a massive explosion erupts from the wreckage, a blinding light as the reactor goes critical from the crash. Overhead sits the Hive ships, command finally loses contact with the Phanes. Planetary cannons are now ordered to open fire up at the aggressors, huge plasma cannons begin to charge, they glow a spectacular blue before opening fire. Beams of plasma lurch up burning the underbellys of one of the closest hive ships. The rounds burn and sear the flesh, liquifying armor and rupturing internals. The hit was seen from the ground, a bright blue glow impacted the hive ship, but even this wasn't able to bring it down, though it looks significantly weakened. The other six begin to unload their pods, these flesh capsules have thick bone beaks containing a complement of around 20 swarmlings shot out from the underbelly of the ships, they rain down like hail. The flyers follow suit and begin tormenting the guns, flak opens up firing at flyers and pods. The pods, though hit heavily by flak, make landfall, their contents spilling out laying waste to any poor soul in proximity. Any form of ground defense is quickly overwhelmed as chaos showers over the planet. Atmospheric fighters face the worst of all threats, above them drop pods become a flight hazard as shriekers and harbingers pick apart any defender still left flying. The skys have fallen to the vorax, and the ground is soon to follow. Fewer and fewer planetary guns fire off into the setting sky, before long, the last remaining guns are silenced, hope has been extinguished, there is no more chance of survival for the people of Scoria. Cities are overwhelmed from the air, and from the land, the vorax are too vicious, and are in numbers no person could count. Evacuation ships could not even get off the ground before being torn apart, not like they would make it to the atmosphere, they had nowhere to go anyways this was their only world. The last of the survivors send out a message, a plea for help knowing none would make it in time, a message to warn the galaxy. A shuttle was launched, rocketing upward and through the carnage. The vorax couldnt sense any sort of life force from the shuttle and did not care for it. The pod broke atmosphere and charged its jump drives before disappearing into the void. Leaving behind a once beautiful world, this craft was the last remaining crumb of the Scorian people, billions of lives and the only thing left to acknowledge their very existence was this insignificant distress probe.

[/spoiler]
